content:
Hi all! I'm preparing some slides for a course on Lean, with quite a lot of Lean code in them.

I tried using Sphinx + sphinx-revealjs, partly because I'd like to stay reasonably close to the ecosystem used for Mathematics in Lean. The setup works nicely, except that I'm struggling to get good syntax highlighting for Lean 4. Reveal.js uses highlight.js, and getting the Lean grammar properly integrated is turning out to be less straightforward than I expected.

Ideally, I'd like something similar to the code highlighting in Mathematics in Lean, but I haven't found an easy way to isolate and reuse the relevant part of its Sphinx setup.

Before I over-engineer this: what do people normally use for slides with Lean code? Any recommended Sphinx setup, or completely different tools/workflows that have worked well for you?
Moritz Doll This looks very interesting, thanks! I'll have a closer look at it now.

@Moritz Doll : It looks excellent and has lots of features that would be extremely useful for teaching Lean — thanks for pointing me to it!

My first impression, though, is that it may still be a bit rough around the edges. Even the example included in the project template doesn't render correctly for me: two of the code boxes overlap (I tried both Safari and Chrome).

I'll play with it a little more, though, because otherwise it looks very promising.
What I like to do is the other way around: Lean code with slides. In particular https://github.com/0art0/lean-slides is the package I use to render slides in the Lean infoview.
Jovan Gerbscheid I wasn't aware of this one either — thanks! I'll have a look at it too.

@Marco Maggesi certainly that's a bug that we are not aware of. Please don't hesitate to open an issue at https://github.com/leanprover/verso-slides/issues/new

If you are interested in Verso Slides, we have a specific #verso channel for focused questions and support.
